title: ophioglossum vulgatum var. crotalophoroides
intro: Ophioglossum vulgatum var. crotalophoroides, commonly known as Adder's Tongue, is a variety of the Adder's Tongue fern, a type of flowering plant that belongs to the family Ophioglossaceae. It has been traditionally used in various cultures for its medicinal properties, offering health benefits such as anti-inflammatory and antibacterial effects, which may aid in wound healing and reducing inflammation. The therapeutic actions of Adder's Tongue include demulcent and vulnerary properties, making it useful in soothing and protecting mucous membranes and promoting tissue repair. The bioactive constituents of Adder's Tongue include saponins, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its potential health benefits and medicinal uses.
